title: RAG hallucination probes — scratchpad and experiment plan
content:
Notes to self — high-level goal:
Goal: build a small, fast evaluation harness that surfaces hallucination modes in RAG pipelines (both generative and extractive answer styles) so we can tune retrieval chunking, reranker strength, and prompt conditioning.

High-level hypotheses (quick):
- Short, high-precision chunks reduce hallucination but hurt recall on multi-hop answers.
- Aggressive reranking (high lambda) reduces unsupported assertions but increases omission (safe-fail).
- Model quantization at q4/q8 may amplify hallucination on synthetic contradiction examples.

Quick reading list (papers / posts to re-check):
- \"Measuring Factuality in RAG\" (arXiv 2025) — metric ideas: Support Ratio, Attribution Precision.
- \"FaithfulQA benchmarks\" — good for baseline; but skewed to closed-book settings.
- \"Paraphrase augmentation for adversarial retrieval\" — useful for synthetic negatives.
- Internal blog: \"retrieval-chunking-postmortem\" (Slack link in #rag-ops) — contains previous flakiness notes.

Initial eval metrics (operational):
- Support Ratio: fraction of generated assertions backed by at least one retrieved chunk (min-high-sim threshold).
- Attribution Precision: among claims that cite a source, fraction that match source text semantically.
- Hallucination Rate: fraction of answers containing at least one unsupported named-entity fact.
- Answer Coverage: macro F1 vs. ground-truth (to measure recall loss from defensive configs).
- Latency and token cost (to trade off economics).

Experiment matrix (fast prototyping plan):
Variables: retrieval chunk size (200/500/1000 tokens), chunk overlap (0/50/200), reranker aggressiveness (0.3/0.7/0.95), response style (extractive / generative), prompt grounding template (explicit-quote / implicit), model variant (llama-2-13b-q8 / redwood-curated-7b-fp16).
Evaluation sets:
- Synthetic contradictions (500 queries): create by paraphrasing evidence and swapping small numeric entities / dates.
- Multi-hop composed QA (200 queries): needs multi-chunk support.
- Real usage sample (200 queries): from internal logs anonymized (see JIRA-RAG-237 for export notes).

Quick dataset construction notes (TODO):
- Script: rag-evals/tools/mk_contradictions.py (WIP). Strategy: take a supporting paragraph, swap an entity (company name / date / amount), rephrase the question so model is likely to hallucinate.
- Add paraphrase augmentation (backtranslation) to make retrieval tougher.
- Label generation: simple heuristics first (string-match + fuzzy match) then small human verification pass (~50 items) to get signal.

Sample prompts (sketch):
- Generative, grounded: \"Use only the retrieved documents to answer. If no document supports the claim, say \'No supported answer\'. Provide endnotes (doc ids) for each assertion.\"
- Extractive (safer): \"Return the best span from retrieved docs. If no span supports the question, return \'NOT_FOUND\'.\"

Practical blocking points and assumptions:
- We rely on retriever similarity scores; need to freeze a similarity threshold for Support Ratio. TODO: decide threshold (0.7/0.8).
- Attribution detection is fuzzy; might need inexpensive NLI scoring or sentence-level embedding alignment. Cost/latency tradeoff.
- Slack/legal: ensure exported queries are anonymized (see privacy checklist in confluence page).

Quick experiments to run this sprint (2-week):
1) Baseline: existing retriever + default chunking (500 tokens overlap 50) + redwood-curated-7b -> run on all three eval sets -> baseline metrics (2 days).
2) Chunk sweep: 200/500/1000 (keep overlap constant) with extractive prompt -> measure hallucination rate + coverage (2 days).
3) Reranker sweep: lambda 0.3/0.7/0.95 with generative-grounded prompt (3 days).
4) Paraphrase-negative augmentation: create 200 synthetic negatives and test retrieval recall (remaining time).

Notes from quick sync (2026-08-04):
- Owen: can add a cheap NLI check using our small 2-class probe to flag contradictions at inference time. Might add signal to Attribution Precision.
- Maya: offered to help label 50 items for validation set on Friday.

Implementation pointers (pragmatic):
- Reuse rag-evals harness in repo: /workspace/rag-evals. Add new config files instead of new harness to keep CI simple.
- Use dedicated small batch of VMs (n1-standard-8) for the sweep; use Redwood Dedicated credits for stable latency measurements.
- Logging: include token-level cost and latency per query in CSV rows (columns: query_id, chunk_config, reranker, model, support_ratio, attr_precision, hallucination_flag, tokens, latency_ms).

Open research questions (free-form):
- Is there a reliable automatic proxy for Attribution Precision that scales cheaply? (embedding alignment? fast NLI? heuristics?).
- How much does chunk overlap mitigate hallucination on multi-hop vs single-hop? Intuition: overlap helps multi-hop continuity but may surface repeated noisy context.
- Are we conflating hallucination with omission (model being cautious)? Need to separate safety-vs-accuracy in labels.

Next steps (concrete):
- Create skeleton configs in rag-evals (this afternoon) -> PR to repo.
- Generate synthetic contradictions (script w/ paraphrase augmentation) -> aim 200 examples by Wed.
- Schedule 30-min sync with Owen + Maya to hand off labeling instructions -> Fri.

Random helpful links / reminders:
- Slack thread: #rag-ops thread id 12345 (contains sample user queries)
- Confluence: RAG Hallucination notes (linked above)
- JIRA: RAG-237 (export queries), RAG-241 (labeling task)

Rough TODO checklist:
- [ ] baseline sweep + upload CSV
- [ ] chunking sweep + chart hallucination vs coverage
- [ ] label 50 validation items
- [ ] prototype cheap attribution scoring

Snippets / quick handoff blurb for PR description (draft):
\"Add RAG hallucination probes: configs for chunking/reranker sweeps and synthetic-contradiction dataset. Outputs CSV with support/attr/hallucination flags to accelerate model+retrieval trade-off analysis.\"

Notes-to-self end — keep this doc mutable. Will split into two polished docs if results look promising (one: methods & metrics; two: usage guidelines for Console teams).
